activities.topic: Introduction to Drones and Basic Flight Concepts

activity_1.title: Look at Flying Things Around You
steps: Go outside or stand near a window and observe the sky.
Find three things that can fly.
Write their names in your notebook.
Observe how they move in the air.

activity_2.title: Paper Helicopter Experiment
steps: Take a piece of paper and cut a strip.
Make two small wings at the top like a propeller.
Fold the bottom to add weight.
Drop it from a small height.
Observe how it spins and falls slowly.
examples: Simple paper helicopter model demonstrating spinning motion

activity_3.title: Imagine a Drone Use in Your Village
steps: Think about a real-life problem in your village or area.
Imagine how a drone could help solve it.
Write one or two sentences explaining your idea.
examples: Example: A drone can fly over farms to check which crops need water.

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone if they have seen a drone in real life.

think_and_notice: Which flying object did you observe?
How do you think drones stay balanced in the air?
How can drones help people in villages?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand basic flying concepts
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how flying objects move in the air.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and curiosity
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze movements of birds, kites, or insects.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect drone technology with real-life problems
learning_outcomes.description: Students imagine how drones can help in agriculture, safety, or delivery.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop creativity and engineering thinking
learning_outcomes.description: Students experiment with simple flying models and ideas.

bonus_activity: Draw a simple drone design in your notebook.
Include four propellers, a body frame, and an optional camera.
Imagine what work your drone would do, such as farming, rescue, or delivery.

activities.topic: Drone Structure, Balance, and Control Systems

activity_1.title: Create a Simple Drone Model
steps: Take cardboard or paper as the main body.
Attach four pencils or sticks in a cross shape.
Draw small circles at the ends to represent motors or propellers.
Observe how the structure is balanced around the center.
examples: Cardboard with four sticks forming a cross structure
Simple drone model showing four propeller positions

activity_2.title: Balance Experiment
steps: Take a ruler or stick.
Place your finger at the center point.
Observe how it balances when weight is equal.
Notice how it tilts when one side becomes heavier.
examples: Tilted ruler when weight is uneven

activity_3.title: Practice Control Movements
steps: Stand in an open space.
Move your hand up to imagine the drone going up.
Move your hand down to imagine the drone going down.
Move your hand forward to imagine forward motion.
Move your hand left or right to imagine direction change.

extra_exploration.task: Find machines at home that use remote control or buttons.

think_and_notice: Why does a drone need four motors instead of one?
What happens if one motor stops working?
Why is balance important for flying machines?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand drone structure
learning_outcomes.description: Students recognize that drones are built from multiple components arranged in balance.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand control systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students learn how remote commands control drone movement.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop basic engineering thinking
learning_outcomes.description: Students build a simple model to understand structure and balance.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect technology concepts with real-life machines
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how remote-controlled devices work in daily life.

bonus_activity: Draw a simple drone control diagram in your notebook.
Label Up (Takeoff), Down (Landing), Left/Right movement, and Forward/Backward movement.
Think about how pilots control drones using joysticks.
